newsitem.title: UK: UK will keep BSE cull decision under review--Hogg.
newsitem.headline: UK will keep BSE cull decision under review--Hogg.

text.p: Britain will keep under review its decision not to proceed with a selective cull of cattle vulnerable to "mad cow" disease in the light of new scientific evidence, agriculture minister Douglas Hogg said on Monday.

Making a statement to parliament, Hogg said: "The Government is not, at least for the time being, proceeding with a selective cull. However, we shall consider the position further in the light of the developing science and other relevant matters."
Britain has agreed to slaughter cattle over 30 months old.

But in September, it refused to go along with the slaughter of a further 147,000 animals deemed most vulnerable to Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy as demanded by its EU partners in return for the lifting of a ban on British beef exports.
This followed an Oxford University report suggesting BSE would die out in Britain by 2001 and that a cull would do little to hasten the disease's demise.
Hogg said he still hoped to persuade Brussels to lift the export ban in respect of herds certified never to have suffered from BSE.
"Clearly if there were a prospect of early progress on exports from certified herds, we would need to take account of this when considering the options for a selective cull," he said.

"Equally if there were to be a clear evidence of maternal transmission (of the disease from cow to calf) -- which for the moment there is not -- we would need to take account of such evidence too when looking at other cull options." -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
